Rachel / team,

Below is a ready-to-drop firewall snippet and the explicit IPs we publish for private-control-plane egress. These are the predictable exit addresses used when Private is configured with "control-plane-proxy: redwood-managed". If Solace chooses customer-managed NAT, they should provide their NAT IPs instead and we will route accordingly.

Allowlist CSV (egress-ip-list.csv) contents (sample rows):
# label,ip,role
control-plane-egress-01,34.201.112.45,control-plane-outbound
control-plane-egress-02,34.201.112.46,control-plane-outbound
control-plane-egress-03,34.201.112.47,control-plane-outbound

Firewall rule snippet (suggested outbound rules to allow on Solace perimeter):
- Source: Private connector subnets (Solace VPC)
- Destination: 34.201.112.45/32, 34.201.112.46/32, 34.201.112.47/32
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS, TLS 1.3 preferred), 853 (DNS over TLS if used for egress DNS)
- Protocols: TCP
- Description: Allow Redwood control-plane API and telemetry egress to Redwood Managed control-plane egress endpoints.

SNI / TLS notes:
- SNI will present hostnames like control.redwood-inference.com or <customer-id>.control.redwood-inference.com depending on tenant config.
- We sign certs via Redwood's CA and support mTLS for customers that enable mutual auth on their control-plane connection.

Provenance & telemetry:
- We log connection start/stop, TLS handshakes (SNI, cert fingerprints), and per-request metadata in audit logs retained per contract.
- For audits we can provide a time-bound authentication/connection report (CSV) showing successful control-plane handshakes for specified date ranges.

Operational caveat: If customer runs strict egress inspection (TLS MITM) they must permit the above SNI names or provide a trusted proxy without terminating client certificate validation.

I can produce the CSV and the policy snippet into the evidence zip.

Jonas
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
